title: pahāna sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.
groupSub: The Nearest Cause for the Origination of dukkha

paras.en:
“Bhikkhus, there are these three vedanā …
The latent tendency to craving should be abandoned in regard to pleasant vedanā.
The latent tendency to aversion should be abandoned in regard to painful vedanā. The latent tendency to ignorance should be abandoned in regard to
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.

When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned the latent tendency to craving in regard to pleasant vedanā,
the latent tendency to aversion in regard to painful vedanā,
and the latent tendency to ignorance in regard to
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā,

then he is called a bhikkhu without latent tendencies,
one who sees rightly. He has cut off craving,
severed the fetters, and by completely breaking through conceit, he has made an end to dukkha.

When one experiences pleasure,
if one does not understand vedanā,
the tendency to craving is present
for one not seeing the way out of it.

When one experiences pain,
if one does not understand vedanā,
the tendency to aversion is present
for one not seeing the way out of it.

The One of Broad Wisdom has taught
with reference to that peaceful vedanā,
neither-painful-nor-pleasant:
if one seeks delight even in this,
one is still not liberated from dukkha.

But when a bhikkhu who is ardent
does not neglect clear comprehension,
then that wise one fully understands
vedanā in their entirety.

Having fully understood vedanā,
he is free from āsavas in this very life.
established in Dhamma, with the body’s breakup
the knowledge-master cannot be described.”
